notYet: Not yet part of the Mediterranean and Persia

stages.name: Major buyer
stages.desc: Courts and elites whose demand drove the trade

stages.name: Dye producer
stages.desc: Phoenician or Punic dye works lead the region's role

stages.name: Phoenician or Punic trader
stages.desc: Phoenician or Punic ports carry the trade; dye works unproven or minor

stages.name: Rival Greek producer
stages.desc: Greek coasts and cities fish and dye their own purple

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Phoenician Kition trades beside the island's Greek kingdoms
Kition's kings conquer Idalion, extending Phoenician power inland
Ptolemy ends Kition's Phoenician dynasty; the island comes under a Greek-Egyptian court

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre and Sidon, vassals of Persia, work the dye vats of the Phoenician coast
Artaxerxes III crushes Sidon's revolt; Diodorus reports more than 40,000 dead
Alexander storms Tyre; Arrian reports 8,000 killed and 30,000 sold into slavery
The coast passes from Ptolemaic to Seleucid rule; the dye works go on

states.name: Syria
timeline: Arwad and the northern Phoenician ports trade and serve in Persia's fleet
After Issus, Arwad submits to Alexander
Seleucus founds Laodicea and Apamea; Seleucid court cities become a market for luxury cloth

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Persian-ruled Anatolia: Greek and Lydian elites prize purple; Colophon is remembered for it
Aristotle records large murex off Sigeum and Lectum and small ones off Caria
Alexander crosses into Asia; the Greek coast changes masters

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, Tyre's western daughter, leads Punic shipping
Murex shells at Kerkouane point to Punic dye making, with salt and fish sauce
Regulus lands at Aspis on Cap Bon; Kerkouane is destroyed or abandoned and never rebuilt
Rome destroys Carthage; shell deposits at Meninx show the dye outlasting it

states.name: Greece
timeline: Hermione and the Laconian coast fish murex and dye their own purple
In Athens, Aeschylus calls purple worth its weight in silver
Plutarch names Hermione, not Tyre, as the source of the purple at Susa
Rome sacks Corinth; the Greek dye coasts pass under Roman power

states.name: Italy
timeline: Etruscan and Italian elites buy eastern luxuries; Pyrgi's tablets show Punic ties
Greek Tarentum grows rich; its Monte dei Coccioli shell heap, undated, marks a purple industry
Rome takes Tarentum; Italy's weight shifts to Rome as a buyer, though Tarentum still dyes
Rome sacks Tarentum after its defection to Hannibal
Macedon's royal treasure enters Rome in the triumph of Aemilius Paullus

states.name: Iran
timeline: The Achaemenid court at Susa and Persepolis, the greatest buyer of all
Alexander takes Susa; Plutarch reports 5,000 talents of purple in the treasury
Alexander's mass weddings at Susa display the seized Persian luxury
Parthian kings take Media from the Seleucids; the eastern market changes hands

states.name: Malta
timeline: A Phoenician colony and safe harbour on the western routes
Rome takes Malta from Carthage; its Punic-speaking weavers stay

events.title: Tyre's dye coast
events.text: Vats of rotting murex line the Phoenician shore; Strabo later says the dye works make Tyre unpleasant to live in, and rich.

events.title: Pyrgi gold tablets
events.text: About 500 BC, an Etruscan ruler at Pyrgi dedicates a shrine in Etruscan and Phoenician, a mark of Punic ties in Italy.

events.title: Battle of Lade
events.text: Phoenician squadrons help Persia crush the Ionian Greek fleet off Miletus.

events.title: Salamis
events.text: Phoenician ships fight for Xerxes and are defeated by the Greek fleet.

events.title: Himera
events.text: Greek Sicilians defeat a Carthaginian army on the island's north coast.

events.title: Eshmunazar's sarcophagus
events.text: About 475 BC, a Sidonian king's coffin text says the Persian king gave Sidon Dor and Joppa on the coast to the south.

events.title: Aeschylus's silver line
events.text: In the Agamemnon, staged at Athens, the sea breeds purple worth its weight in silver.

events.title: Kition takes Idalion
events.text: About 450 BC, the Phoenician kings of Kition conquer the Cypriot kingdom of Idalion.

events.title: Kerkouane's shells
events.text: Murex shells and possible vats at this Punic town suggest dye making on Cap Bon; the dating is loose.

events.title: Motya sacked
events.text: Dionysius of Syracuse storms the Punic island town of Motya in western Sicily and kills or enslaves its people.

events.title: Tarentum's purple
events.text: Tarentum grows rich; a shell heap known as Monte dei Coccioli later marks its dye industry, though it is undated.

events.title: Athens honours Strato
events.text: About 367 BC, Athens honours Sidon's king and eases taxes on Sidonian merchants; the decree's date is debated.

events.title: Rome–Carthage treaty
events.text: A second treaty sets limits on Roman trade in Carthaginian waters.

events.title: Sidon burns
events.text: About 345 BC, Artaxerxes III retakes rebel Sidon; Diodorus reports more than 40,000 dead in the fire.

events.title: Aristotle's purple fishers
events.text: Living at Assos near Cape Lectum in the 340s BC, Aristotle records large murex there and how fishers extract the dye.

events.title: Alexander enters Asia
events.text: Alexander crosses the Hellespont and the Persian Empire begins to fall.

events.title: Arwad submits
events.text: After Issus, the Phoenician island of Arwad surrenders to Alexander.

events.title: Tyre stormed
events.text: After a seven-month siege; Arrian reports 8,000 killed and 30,000 sold into slavery.

events.title: Treasure of Susa
events.text: Alexander takes Susa; Plutarch reports 5,000 talents of purple, but Diodorus's tally of the treasure mentions none.

events.title: Hermione's purple
events.text: Plutarch says the Susa purple came from Hermione and had been stored for 190 years.

events.title: Persepolis plundered
events.text: Diodorus says rich dresses of sea purple became the prize of Alexander's soldiers.

events.title: Theopompus names the price
events.text: About this time, Theopompus recalls Colophon's thousand men in purple, then sold for its weight in silver.

events.title: Susa weddings
events.text: Alexander stages mass marriages of Macedonian officers to Persian noblewomen.

events.title: Kition's last king
events.text: Ptolemy has Kition's last Phoenician king killed and takes the city.

events.title: Agathocles in Africa
events.text: A Greek army from Sicily invades Carthage's Cap Bon heartland.

events.title: Laodicea founded
events.text: About 300 BC, Seleucus founds a port on the Syrian coast, part of a new chain of court cities.

events.title: Ptolemy's pavilion
events.text: About this time, Ptolemy II's feast pavilion at Alexandria is laid with rugs of purple, as a later writer records.

events.title: Tarentum falls
events.text: Rome takes Tarentum after the war with Pyrrhus, and southern Italy's dye coast with it.

events.title: War over Messana
events.text: Rome and Carthage go to war for the first time over Sicily.

events.title: Regulus lands
events.text: A Roman army lands at Aspis on Cap Bon and ravages the coast.

events.title: Kerkouane destroyed
events.text: About this time the town is destroyed or abandoned; it is never rebuilt, so its plan survives.

events.title: Aegates Islands
events.text: Carthage loses the sea battle and the First Punic War, and gives up Sicily.

events.title: Malta falls
events.text: At the start of the Second Punic War, Rome takes Malta from its Carthaginian garrison.

events.title: Tarentum sacked
events.text: Fabius retakes the city after its defection; Livy reports 30,000 sold into slavery.

events.title: Zama
events.text: Scipio defeats Hannibal in North Africa, ending the war and Carthage's overseas power.

events.title: Battle of Panium
events.text: Antiochus III defeats the Ptolemies; Tyre and Sidon pass to Seleucid rule.

events.title: Triumph of Paullus
events.text: Macedon's royal treasure is paraded through Rome after the conquest of Perseus.

events.title: Delos a free port
events.text: Rome makes Delos a free port, drawing eastern merchants to the Aegean.

events.title: Parade at Daphne
events.text: Antiochus IV stages a vast parade near Antioch, with robes embroidered in gold on the images of the gods.

events.title: Tyrian merchants' guild
events.text: On Delos, an association of Tyrian merchants and shippers honours its priest with a gold crown.

events.title: Meninx on Djerba
events.text: Undated shell deposits mark this Punic port, whose purple Pliny later ranks next after Tyre's.

events.title: Parthians take Media
events.text: About this time, Mithridates I wrests Media from the Seleucids.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Rome razes Carthage and makes its territory the province of Africa.

events.title: Corinth sacked
events.text: In the same year, Rome destroys Corinth and takes control of Greece.

chartNote: Share of the area of nine present-day countries, by each one's main role in the purple trade; regions are today's boundaries. This is a simplification: every region held several roles at once, and many shell heaps and vats are only loosely dated. Vast Iran and Turkey swing the shares, while tiny Lebanon, the industry's heart, barely registers. Israel and Egypt, also part of the story, are not coloured.
